Would like to finish a bit of drywall. It's just been sitting there for a while but I'd like to finally get it painted and trimmed. I don't have any drywall mud or tape here, but I do have a big bucket of lightweight spackle that I don't need. I think it's more than enough to fill in the gaps and screw holes.

If I just spackle and paint it, is something bad gonna happen? Like cracks or something? The wall is on concrete and it's been sitting for like a year, so I don't think it's going to settle much if at all.
Can I finish drywall with lightweight spackle?
It will most likely crack along the joints without tape, especially if wall is load bearing, double especially if house is on piers instead of slab/full foundation.
You need to tape it first, that's how you prevent cracking. Then put on thin coats of spackle, let it dry, sand, and apply again.

Personally, I wouldn't ever use lightweight spackle for that particular application. I would use it for minor cosmetic defects but basically anything like seams or joints, I'd use actual joint compound.

[Meta] Table Manners at The Dinner Table & the Meaning of "Civil Discourse"

I like that I can converse in an informed and polite way here, with anyone, whatever their views, and get a polite and informed response, no matter what the subject. I would not like to see the name calling and condescending responses I see elsewhere.

If I do not understand your point of view, please explain it. Many of us come from different societies so do not have ANY idea of what is offensive in your society. For example, I live in the UK, but recently found out that 'Mick' was supposed to be a term of abuse against the Irish. Believe me, it is not, in Ireland at least (or to my Irish friends anyway). In the same spirit of understanding, I would hope that you would not get offended by my using the word e.g.Mick, but ask me why and enter into a discourse.

Civil discourse, for me is about not taking offense, but asking questions to find out why that person has that point of view and learning about another persons point of view. Of course, you may still disagree, but the language will not have gotten in the way, and, hopefully, we can both try to convert each other to each othres point of view.
